assessments.reasoning: The verified 704-byte range at the full-copy-only anchor in the pinned Mozilla Bedrock template contains the question, the attachment explanation and the historical exception. Mozilla identifies the FAQ as guidance. Its authority suffices for the claim about what Mozilla documented.

challenge.method: Held the accompanying document constant and varied two facts independently: actual attachment of Exhibit B by the initial Contributor, and an upgrade from MPL 1.1-only licensing.
challenge.results: Actual attachment supplies the separate section 1.5(a) ground. An MPL 1.1-only history can establish section 1.5(b) despite the absence of attachment. Both cases are consistent with Q25’s narrower observation about an exhibit printed inside a license copy.

limitations: This is a documented explanation of one scenario. Its legal meaning depends on the underlying MPL. Section 1.5(b) extends to version 1.1 or earlier and asks whether the software was also available under a defined Secondary License.
Q25 does not establish the licensing history of particular code or resolve standalone redistribution of the license document.
reasoning: Q25 addresses code shipped with the full MPL 2.0 document and without per-file boilerplate. Mozilla explains that Exhibit B’s presence inside that document does not itself attach the notice to the source.
